title: Topic 11 · Government Governance and Public Spending
blocks: h2

ul

**legislation** (আইন প্রণয়ন): New legislation was passed to curb pollution.
**bureaucracy** (আমলাতন্ত্র): Excessive bureaucracy slows down public services.
**subsidy** (ভর্তুকি): Fuel subsidies keep transport affordable for the poor.
**taxation** (করারোপ): Progressive taxation redistributes wealth.
**accountability** (জবাবদিহিতা): Voters demand greater accountability from officials.
**welfare** (জনকল্যাণ): The welfare system supports the unemployed.
**expenditure** (ব্যয়): Public expenditure on health has risen steadily.
**transparency** (স্বচ্ছতা): Transparency reduces the scope for corruption.
**policy** (নীতি): Sound economic policy underpins stable growth.
h2

ul

**subsidise** (subsidised, subsidised, subsidising): The state subsidises public transport.
**legislate** (legislated, legislated, legislating): Parliament legislated against child labour.
**govern** (governed, governed, governing): A stable coalition now governs the country.
**impose** (imposed, imposed, imposing): The government imposed a tax on sugary drinks.
**prioritise** (prioritised, prioritised, prioritising): Officials must prioritise essential services.
**fund** (funded, funded, funding): The state fully funds primary schooling.
**reform** (reformed, reformed, reforming): The new minister pledged to reform the tax system.
h2
Collocations and adjectives (10)
ul
**public spending**: Public spending on healthcare must rise. (Writing)
**tax revenue**: Tax revenue funds essential services. (Writing)
**welfare state**: The welfare state protects the most vulnerable. (Writing)
**government intervention**: Government intervention is sometimes unavoidable. (Writing)
**fiscal policy**: Sound fiscal policy controls inflation. (Writing)
**red tape**: Businesses complain about excessive red tape. (Speaking and Writing)
**accountable to the public**: Officials must remain accountable to the public. (Writing)
**public services**: Reliable public services improve daily life. (Speaking and Writing)
**state-funded**: State-funded universities widen access. (Writing)
**budget deficit**: A large budget deficit limits future spending. (Writing)

**impose higher taxes**: One option is to impose higher taxes on the wealthy.

ul

blocks.title: Exercise 4.13.3 · Speaking Simulation Drill
blocks.instructions: Answer each Part 3 question in two to three sentences, using at least one target idiom and one collocation. Then compare with the model answer.

items.prompt: Do you think the generation gap is bigger today than in the past?
items.answer: The generation gap does feel wider today, largely because technology moves so fast that parents and teenagers do not always see eye to eye, though open conversation can still bridge it.

items.prompt: Who has more influence on children, parents or friends?
items.answer: Both matter, but as children grow, peer pressure often outweighs parental guidance; even so, parents remain the first role models and shape a child’s core values.

items.prompt: Is it better to grow up in a large family or a small one?
items.answer: There are trade-offs either way; a large family offers close-knit support, whereas a small one may allow more quality time and resources per child, so neither is simply better.

blocks.instructions: Answer each Part 3 question in two to three sentences, using at least one target idiom and one collocation. Then compare with the model answer.

items.prompt: Why do you think international travel has become so popular?
items.answer: International travel has boomed because it broadens people’s horizons and offers a welcome change of scenery; once you catch the travel bug, exploring new destinations becomes hard to resist.

items.prompt: Does tourism do more good or harm to a country?
items.answer: It does both; tourism can boost the local economy and promote cultural understanding, yet mass tourism puts a strain on local resources and can degrade the very attractions people come to see.

items.prompt: Do you prefer package holidays or independent travel?
items.answer: I lean toward independent travel, because it lets you get off the beaten track and immerse yourself in local life, though a package holiday is more convenient if you are short on time.
